## The `4^-t` sparsity of the reachable rows is exact, global and computable, and it permits rows of black density 0.97

**The natural attempt.** The entry above this one about the row marginal ends
by naming the one thing it does not cover. Rule 30 is pre-injective (crystal 4),
so the map from a finite configuration of span `m` to the row it becomes after
`t` steps is injective, and only `2^(m-2)` of the `2^(m+2t-2)` black-ended words
of span `m + 2t` occur — a `4^-t`-sparse set, two bits of information destroyed
per step. That is a genuine, quantitative, provable constraint on a row, and it
is the precise sense in which the row is not free where crystal 40 makes the
centre column free. So use it: find a word that is *not* a `t`-step image, and
more to the point find the density ceiling it must impose, which would sharpen
`2b(t+1) + 3b(t) ≤ 6t + 9` below its `3/5` and reach row balance.

**Why it fails, and each half is measured.**

*The window reading has no negative at all, and that is a construction rather
than a measurement.* Every word of every length occurs as a **window** of row
`t` of a finite configuration, for every `t`: solve rule 30 leftward `t` times
from the word with the free cells set white, pad the result with white on both
sides, and the light cone (`evolveFrom_eq_of_agree_on_window`, proved) makes the
padding irrelevant. Verified over **688,110 `(t, word)` pairs** at `t ≤ 8` and
word lengths to 16, 0 failures, and independently by brute-force factor sweep
over every finite configuration of span `≤ 18` (`256/256` words of length 8 at
`t = 3,4,5,6`); kernel instance `k1_window` in
`explorer/sextant9_scratch_reach.lean`, axioms `[propext]`
(`explorer/sextant9_window.mjs`). The half that does the work is in print twice
— Wolfram 1986 §4 lines 447–456 and Fukś 2013 §2 line 75, both the
four-preimages leftward solve — and the new part is only the step from blocks to
finite configurations, which is the cone.

*So the constraint is a whole-row statement, and as a whole-row statement it
imposes no density ceiling.* Take the window to be all-black of length `L`: the
same construction gives a finite configuration of span `L + 2t` whose row `t`
has span `L + 4t` and contains `L` consecutive black cells, so its black density
is at least `L/(L + 4t) → 1`. Measured at `t = 40`, `L = 4000`: **row density
`0.971875`** with the 4000-cell black run verified present by forward evolution;
`0.987943` at `t = 16` and `0.999500` at `t = 1`
(`explorer/sextant9_maxdensity.mjs`, 24 `(t, L)` pairs, run present in all).
Separately the `3/5` witness is itself a reachable row at every depth: the ring
`10011` planted as a genuine finite configuration of span 200,001 has middle
density `0.600002` at every `t ≤ 60` (`explorer/sextant9_fence.mjs`). **So
conditioning the row bound on "this row is a `t`-step image" cannot move `3/5`,
and Prize 2 gets nothing from the sparsity.**

**What the constraint actually is, because it is exactly describable and that is
worth recording rather than losing.** A finite configuration has at most one
*finite* predecessor and there is a one-pass procedure that finds it: the only
right tail consistent with white-far-right is the white one, so left-permutivity
forces every cell going leftward with no choice anywhere. Past the left end of
the support the recursion degenerates to `x(i-1) = x(i) | x(i+1)`, which is
white for ever if the two cells immediately left of the support came out white
and **black for ever otherwise**. So finiteness of the predecessor is exactly
two bits, and they sit at the **left edge**; iterating `t` times decides
membership in `O(t · n)`. Checked against brute force over **2,258,262 words**,
every `t ≤ 6` and every span to 20, **0 disagreements** in either direction, with
the count `2^(n-2t-2)` exact at every `(t, n)` and finite-preimage uniqueness at
2,048 images (`explorer/sextant9_criterion.mjs`). Three cautions with it. The
`1/4` survival rate per backward step is the count restated and is evidence of
nothing. That the constraint *exists* is classical — Amoroso–Cooper's
Garden-of-Eden theorem for finite configurations (reference [29] of
`sources/martinez-adamatzky-hoffmann-rule22.txt`, the paper not held): rule 30
is not injective (crystal 5), hence not surjective on finite configurations —
and it must not be reported as a finding. And the criterion is **not** a cone-edge
condition: `11101` has the legal prefix of the reachable `11011` and the legal
suffix of the reachable `11001` and is row 1 of no finite configuration
(hand-verified, and `k2_unreachable` in the kernel file above over every
configuration supported in `[-3,7]`, with `explorer/sextant9_scratch_mutant.lean`
beside it rejected by Lean at the right line). No prefix-plus-suffix condition of
any width cuts out the reachable set, at any `t ≤ 7`
(`explorer/sextant9_nonlocal.mjs`), and at depth 8 flipping **any** single cell
anywhere in the row destroys reachability with probability `≥ 0.99`.

**One cross-vocabulary confirmation and one discrepancy, both worth an hour to
whoever cares.** The reachable set at depth `t` is a regular language — read
right-to-left carrying the `t` backward-solve levels as state — and its minimal
automaton has `3, 7, 16, 35, 71, 141, 272, 517, 971, 1792, 3263, 5873, 10483,
18619, 32885, 57741, 100901, 175680, 304714, 526563` states at `t = 1…20`,
ratios falling from `2.33` to `1.728` (`explorer/sextant9_automaton.mjs`,
`sextant9_automaton2.mjs`; cross-checked against the backward-solve decider over
every word of length `2t+8` for `t ≤ 6`, the only disagreement being the
all-white word, and against brute-force configuration counts at ten `(t, span)`
pairs). **Those are the numbers of the entry "The rule 30 edge group is not
contracting"**, whose forced-set sizes are `35, 532, 5873, 57741, 175680` at
`ℓ = 4, 8, 12, 16, 18`: four of five agree exactly, including both six-digit
entries, from code sharing nothing with `nucleus_*.cjs` and a framing with no
group in it. The fifth does not — **517 here against 532 there at `ℓ = t = 8`** —
and I cannot say which is right without reading that code; my ratios are smooth
across that point (`1.901, 1.878, 1.846`) and theirs jump (`1.97` then `1.82`),
which is weak evidence for 517 and weak is all it is. The consequence either way
is the same and it is the honest answer to "is there a computable description of
the reachable set at all": **yes, a finite automaton for each `t`, and no uniform
one**, since a bounded description would make that group contracting.

**A cross-check that was not looked for, and is the cleanest thing here.** The
all-black word of span `n` is a 1-step image of a finite configuration **exactly
when `3 | n`**, with preimage `(100)^k`, for every `n` from 3 to 22
(`explorer/sextant9_allblack.mjs`) — which is crystal 25's ring Garden-of-Eden
result (Wolfram 1986 §9, crediting the Feynmans) reproduced under a *different
boundary condition*. At `t = 2` the all-black row is a 2-step image at no span
`≤ 24`, which is the previous entry's "`(100)^k` is a dead end" from the other
side.

**Consequence for a seeder.** A P2 proposal that leans on the row being a
`t`-step image is refuted in advance by the density measurement above, exactly
as crystal 40 refutes a P2 proposal about the centre column that does not name
the cone. What is worth seeding out of this is one node and it is a fence: *every
word occurs as a window of row `t` of a finite configuration*, size M, needing
crystal 3 (four preimages / the leftward solve) seeded first — the second attack
document to want that crystal — and it must land with its `DOES NOT PROVE` field
saying that it makes the `4^-t` sparsity invisible to every bounded-window
argument, since that is its entire value.

3. **Nothing, for P1, and the reason is quantitative.** Read as a condition on

## 1. The residual, in one paragraph

Time runs down the picture. `centerColumn k` is the cell at the origin at row
`k`, and it is simultaneously index `0` of left diagonal `k` — where it sits
inside a transient nobody can bound — and index `0` of **right diagonal** `k`,
where the diagonal is exactly periodic with period `2^k` from its very first
cell and has no transient at all. That is why crystal 70 called the right edge
a better position for P1. Obstruction 8 then closed the position from one side:
the tower of right diagonals is generated by the recurrence from `R_0`, `R_1`
and one free bit per level, that free bit *is* the centre column, and the
configuration `…10101|000` — the `(01)^ℤ` fixed point meeting white at the
origin — shares with the seed its recurrence, its two edge diagonals and its
initial row at every `x ≥ 0` while having a flat tower of period 2 at every
depth. Its verdict: the property that separates the seed from that witness is
the existence of a **leftmost black cell**, and that "lives outside the tower".
The residual of P1 at this edge is therefore: find a statement about the right
diagonals that the seed satisfies and the flat tower does not, that is weak
enough to be a hypothesis rather than a restatement of the initial row, and
strong enough that a periodic centre column would contradict it. This document
writes the separating statement down, proves it, and shows it is not weak.

## 2. Why the known routes fail

**Obstruction 8 (the flat tower is a real picture).** No property of the
recurrence, the two edge diagonals, the initial row at `x ≥ 0`, or any
statistic of the right half decides whether the right-diagonal periods grow,
because `…10101|000` shares all of them. Amended here in its letter and
confirmed in its spirit: C2 and §4.

**Obstruction 17 (unbounded right-diagonal periods do not force an aperiodic
centre column).** The converse half: `b = (1000)^∞` gives a tower reaching
minimal period `2^27` by depth 64 with doubling density `0.406`, identical to
the seed's to three digits. So even a sharp theorem about the period growth
buys nothing for P1. Untouched here; this document is about the *cone*, not
about the periods — and C3 is precisely such a sharp theorem, which is why it
is filed as supply rather than as progress.

**Obstruction 7 (a universal argument over periodic words cannot give
minimality).** Its witnesses are arbitrary pairs of periodic words, and
obstruction 17's correction notes none is reachable as a consecutive pair in an
actual tower. Not engaged, and C3 sidesteps it: `edge_gap_eq` quantifies over
the *minimal* period directly rather than over the doubling criterion's
even-branch minimality, which obstruction 7 leaves open.

**Obstruction 1 (the diagonal structure never reaches the centre column).**
Its last sentence is the trap this topic aimed at: the left-diagonal recurrence
"closes on the very cell it was meant to explain". The right-side recurrence
closes the same way — `R_k(0)` is the free coordinate — and running it backwards
does **not** escape that (C5).

**Crystal 69 (the centre column outruns the settling front).** A fence on the
packed-row side; not engaged, since the right diagonals have no settling front.

**Obstructions 9 and 20 (no statistic of the half-line separates the seed from
an arbitrary boundary).** These are why C5 reads as a fence rather than a step:
the cone condition *is* a separating statement, and its price is that it is not
a statistic at all but a recursion that pins the boundary bit by bit.

**A route I considered and discarded on paper, before measuring.** Pair the
cone condition at level `k` with the doubling criterion at level `k+2`: both
are parities of the *same* driver `g_k(j) = R_{k-1}(j+1) | R_{k-2}(j+2)`, one
over the `k` indices at the end of a period (C4) and one over a whole period.
There are 21 doubling depths below `2^21` and no null model survives 21
samples; my own notebook records "a striking constant measured at one `n`" as
this project's most repeated error, so I did not measure it. Recorded so the
next session does not either without a bigger sample.

**New dead end, appended to `docs/obstructions.md`** as *"The cone condition
does live inside the right-diagonal tower, and having it is having the centre

> Let `P_d` be the minimal period of right diagonal `d`. If `P_d ∣ p` for every

### C4 — the telescoped identity: the centre column is a parity along the backward line

**The claim.** Right diagonal `k` at index `-i` is the cell `(k-i, -i)`, so
running level `k` backwards walks the line `x = t - k` from the centre-column
cell `(k, 0)` up to the initial row at `(0, -k)`. Telescoping the rule along
that line, with the initial row white at `-k`:

> for every `k ≥ 1`,
> `centerColumn k = XOR over s < k of ( evolve s (s-k+1) OR evolve s (s-k+2) )`.

Each term is the OR of two **horizontally adjacent** cells of row `s`, so it is
`0` exactly at a white pair, and the identity reads
`centerColumn k ≡ k + #{white pairs along the line} (mod 2)`.

### C5 — as a condition on the free bits, it is affine in the top bit and of near-maximal degree

**The claim.** Within crystal 40's family write `F_k(b_0, …, b_k) := X_b(-k)`,
so the cone condition at level `k` is `F_k = 0`. Then, measured exactly:
- `F_k = b_k ⊕ G_k(b_0, …, b_{k-1})` — **affine in its top variable at every
  `k ≤ 17`**, so level `k` determines `b_k` from the levels below it;
- `deg F_k` is `1, 1, 2, 2, 4, 5, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16` for
  `k = 1..17`: **`≈ 0.87 k`, near-maximal**;
- the ANF support is `43,508` of the `2^18` monomials at `k = 17`, a density of
  **`0.166`, stable over `k = 9..17` (`0.156`–`0.171`, no trend)**, against
  `0.5` for a random function;
- the levels are **independent**: any subset `S` cuts the free bits by exactly
  `|S|`, and the full family `k = 1..K` leaves exactly **two** solutions — the
  all-white configuration and the seed.

**Band: novel as a measurement, and a fence rather than a step.** Nobody has
measured it. What it measures is that the topic's third death mode fires.

**What it would give.** The verdict on the topic. The condition is not trivially
satisfied (C2's flat-tower half; and a random `b` violates it at mean level
`2.0162` against a coin's `2.0`, with the whole histogram a coin's). It is not
merely the forward evolution restated cell for cell — it is a genuine recursion,
and a *sparse* subfamily of levels excludes the flat tower while leaving the
centre column massively underdetermined. But its degree grows linearly and its
ANF has about `2^k / 6` monomials, so no argument is going to use it. And the
fence is sharper than "unusable": because the levels are independent and each
spends one bit, **a cofinite subfamily determines the centre column from a
finite prefix of itself** — which is precisely "white far to the left", and
precisely why having the separating property in the tower's language is having
the centre column.

**Falsification.** `explorer/sextant10_conefn.mjs`. The solver is the board's

construction rather than of rule 30. Control, and it is crystal 66's own

the shape of the solver. The ANF density `0.166` I report as an **observation
with no theory**: it is exact, stable over nine values with no trend, a random

## 4. What survived

All five survived, and the two that are **proved rather than proposed** are the
deliverable. **Seed C2 and C3 together**: `cone_row` and `cone_rightDiagonal`
give crystal 11's blocked ingredient, and `edge_gap_eq` gives crystal 12's
computed mirror half, with a rejected-mutant companion and a `decide`
cross-check against `rowCell`. Crystal 11's conclusion ("rows `2^n - 1` and
`2^n` restart the right edge") has sat unseeded since 2026-09-07 because its
second ingredient was priced as Rowland's induction; it costs three closed
nodes and a least-element argument. The one generic lemma the board lacks is
`rd_periodicFrom_minimalPeriod` — that a minimal period *is* a period, two
lines from `Nat.sInf_mem` — and it is worth seeding on its own, since every
statement about `minimalPeriod` on this board currently has to route around it.
C1 is the bridge and wants one definition; C4 wants a fold; C5 cannot be a node.

**The topic's question, answered.** Yes: the cone condition is a statement the
board can carry, it needs no new definition, and it is
`rightDiagonal k (2^k - k) = false`. Obstruction 8's verdict is wrong in its
letter — the separating property does **not** live outside the tower — and right
in its spirit, for a reason it did not state and I did not expect. The
condition is not a weak structural property of the tower that could be
leveraged against a periodic centre column. It is **one independent bit of
constraint per level, affine in exactly the free bit of that level**, so the
whole family is equivalent to "the configuration is the seed" and a cofinite
subfamily to "the configuration is number-like, with the centre column
determined by a finite prefix of itself". The residual at the right edge is
therefore unchanged in content and clarified in form: P1 asks whether a sequence
satisfying a specific nonlinear recursion — degree `≈ 0.87 k` at level `k`, ANF
density `1/6` — can be eventually periodic. Nothing about that shape is easier
than P1, and the degree is why.

One thing I am **not** claiming, and it is the temptation this document is
closest to: that the cone condition is useless. It is what crystals 11 and 12
need, it is exactly tight, and the right-diagonal region gains four or five
proved nodes and a printed theorem. What it does not gain is a handle on the
centre column.
